Let $A$ be a finite abelian group. The set $V_A = A \oplus \widehat{A}$ is equipped with a natural symplectic form given by $\langle (a, \chi), (a', \chi') \rangle = \chi(a') - \chi'(a)$.
The Clifford group $C(A)$ is a subgroup of the group of symplectic similitudes of $V_A$ (or related to the affine group depending on convention, but here it acts on the Heisenberg group structure). Specifically, $C(A)$ fits into the central extension:
\[ 1 \to V_A \to C(A) \to \Sp(V_A) \to 1 \]
The splitting of this sequence is equivalent to the existence of a subgroup of $C(A)$ isomorphic to $\Sp(V_A)$ that maps isomorphically onto the quotient. In other words, does there exist a homomorphism $s: \Sp(V_A) \to C(A)$ such that the composition $\Sp(V_A) \xrightarrow{s} C(A) \to \Sp(V_A)$ is the identity?
